test_title: RRB NTPC CBT-I Official Paper (Held On: 8 Mar 2021 Shift 1)
subject: general
question:
Study the following pie chart carefully which shows the monthly expenditure (in ₹) of a family.

If total amount spent on monthly expenditure during the month was ₹45,000, then what was the amount (in ₹) spent on education and health taken together (to the nearest thousand)?

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ae3b5983fbae6cdd5fcb7e6e055258040061f4d19c379ab31ed57c886ceed1fa.png]
solution:
**Given:**

Total monthly expenditure = ₹45,000

Education = 2.5 parts

Health = 2 parts

**Formula used:**

Total amount spent on Education and Health together = dfrac{(Education + Health)}{Total parts} times Total expenditure 

**Calculation:**

Total parts = 3.5 (Food) + 2.3 (House rent) + 2.5 (Education) + 2 (Health) + 1.9 (Entertainment) + 1 (Fuel) + 0.5 (Bill payment) = 13.7

Amount spent on Education and Health = dfrac{(2.5 + 2)}{13.7} times 45,000

⇒ dfrac{4.5}{13.7} times 45,000 = 14,781.75

⇒ Amount ≈ ₹15,000 (to the nearest thousand)

**∴ The amount spent on education and health together is ₹15,000.**
